text: Muscae Volitantes [Lat. musca , a fly, + volitans , dancing]; Ger. fliegende Mücken ; Fr. mouches volantes ; Ital. mosche volanti . Variable entoptic appearances, due to the presence of small foreign bodies in the vitreous humour. They take the form of bright worm-like threads, strings of glistening beads, groups of bright dots, tiny circles with brighter centres, &c., and usually travel downward in the field of vision (i.e. upward in the humour). Cf. ENTOPTIC PHENOMENA. Literature : HELMHOLTZ, Physiol. Optik. (2nd ed.) 188; SANFORD, Course in Exper. Psychol., expt. 110. ( E.B.T. )
